problem: How many different ways can a group of four be made from a room of eighty people?

feedback.problem: How many different ways can a team of four be made from a class of twelve students?
feedback.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $12$ students, so $n=12.$ We want to select $4$ of those students for the team, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different potential teams of four is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{12}{C}_{4} & =\frac{12!}{(12-4)!\,4!} \\  & =\frac{12!}{8!4!} \\  & =\frac{12\cdot 11\cdot 10\cdot 9\cdot \cancel{8!}}{\cancel{8!}4!} \\  & =\frac{12\cdot 11\cdot 10\cdot 9}{4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{11\,880}{24} \\  & =495.\end{aligned}
$$
